goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — Removing isSenderIdNeeded from the outer (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) condition plus unrelated JSX re-indentation/unwrapping is scope creep bundled into a commit whose stated purpose is workflow reminder lifecycle management, hurting traceability

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `WorkflowStepContainer.tsx` changes the render condition from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` only, and also rewrites/re-indents the JSX within that block. This is a UI-scope change mixed into a PR whose other hunks are about workflow reminder cancellation/lifecycle (email/SMS reminder managers, cancellation flags, reschedule cleanup). Bundling an unrelated UI conditional change and JSX restructuring with backend reminder lifecycle work reduces traceability and makes review/rollback harder. The finding is grounded in the shown change at the indicated area.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Cancellation loop awaits `client.request(...)` to SendGrid one reminder at a time inside a `for` loop instead of batching/parallelizing, so cron runtime grows linearly with the number of cancelled reminders and delays the subsequent unscheduled-reminder scheduling in the same invocation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic does `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... }`, which serializes SendGrid cancellation requests one-by-one. This makes the handler’s runtime scale linearly with the number of reminders and can delay the subsequent "find all unscheduled Email reminders" scheduling work in the same invocation. It’s a concrete performance/scalability concern shown by the diff, not a direct correctness break on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:75 — The outer catch only does `console.log`, so a partial-failure/idempotency bug in the cancel-reminders block (see above) is silently swallowed with no alerting, retry-with-backoff, or per-item isolation, letting one bad reminder permanently block progress on the batch

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancel block wraps the entire cancellation loop in a single `try/catch` that only `console.log`s on error. Because each reminder cancellation does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop, a single failing reminder will throw and immediately jump to the outer `catch`, skipping cancellation/deletion of any remaining `remindersToCancel`. With no per-item isolation, retry, or marking, the same bad reminder could repeatedly cause the block to bail out early on subsequent runs, leaving later reminders unprocessed.
